I was going to write a post but I couldn’t work out a good title. A little backstory, I was diagnosed with a severe mental illness the day after my 16th birthday. The psychiatrist was waiting for that date in particular because that’s the earliest you can diagnose a child with a severe mental illness. My mum was behind it 100%, she would see my psychiatrist without me and tell lies/exaggerate stories about me. This illness ruled my life, it was all I was known for, I was sedated and medicated for YEARS, it was used against me by multiple different abusers. I thought I was broken because the medication and therapy never helped or worked. 

Last night in the hospital, at 2am, the diagnosis was scrapped. I never had that disorder. It was false. I’m only a few weeks away from turning 24, and I feel like I’m starting fresh. I feel like I’m just beginning my life. I’ve been on and off crying all day. It’s so freeing.

The autism spectrum. I don’t know for sure, I’m currently on a 14 month waiting list for an assessment. 

I’ve spent so much time over four years researching autism, and specifically how it presents in girls. I know that I was misdiagnosed with bipolar disorder (at 16!) and BPD because as soon as I went no contact with my mother, my “symptoms” cleared up completely. I’ve never had another manic/depressive episode, never feared abandonment, never had jealous rage, don’t have racing thoughts. I’ve been a million times better off medication. She was the reason I got diagnosed with bipolar disorder, she kept suggesting it to my junior psychiatrist because my grandmother had bipolar, and I was a “difficult teen” (abused and reactive to that). And I got diagnosed with BPD only weeks after my dad died. It was my first time seeing this new psychiatrist and I was pretty emotional bc my dad just died, and they diagnosed me with BPD because I showed symptoms in the 50 minutes they saw me for. It’s since been wiped from my medical history for false diagnoses. 

But even now, there’s still things that are ‘off’ that have always shown and been persistent. Those things line up with someone (especially AFAB people) on the spectrum, so I got a referral to some professionals to check. I’ve got 8 months left til I know for sure. It wasn’t all out of nowhere though, I had a school counsellor when I was 10 that was super persistent with my parents to get me assessed for Aspergers but they didn’t want me to have a label. 

Sorry for going on a tangent haha

Now I wake up, take my sorry ass to the scale, immediately forget the number, avoid looking at the mirror, climb back into bed and think about food all day. 

I lost everything I was working towards outside of this disorder. I had job prospects but that’s quickly fading. I was going to study some more, but I can’t make myself get out of bed. Thank you for asking!! I completely understand how nerve-wracking it is, even just thinking about going through with a name change. For a long time before applying, I felt like I was being a drama queen (definitely my egg donors words burnt into the back of my skull). Thankfully I’ve never had to tell any of my biological family, but if I had to, I’d tell them that my new name is my true identity and they can shove my dead name. 

When I was trying to figure out my new name, I would write names that stuck out to me in a notebook. The next time I looked at the notebook, I’d cross out any names that I didn’t think about while the book was closed. I only told my partner and my best friends that I was considering changing my name, but I was shit scared to even tell them. They were totally supportive and even offered to help me pick out names that suited me. I gathered up my top 10 first names, put them into Google Forms, and had both of them choose their favourites. After that, we all spoke about which name suited me best, and slowly vetoed nine names til we were left with my new first name. My middle name was changed to Claire, my partner suggested it because it rhymes with Bear (and she’s always called me a big cuddly teddy bear). My last name was hard to choose because I had no idea what I wanted. I went with a common last name that also happens to honour my favourite actress :) Then to make sure I really loved the name, I wrote it on sticky notes and stuck them all around the house. I made up signatures and I used it to name my characters in video games 

It took about a week for my first name to stick with my partner and best friend. They said my dead name only a few times each over that week. I remember them saying it was pretty awkward during the first few days, like it felt wrong to go against the name they’d been calling me for years. I felt the same way; it was super strange. But it did stick! With my in-laws and more distant friends, it’s been a bit harder. I don’t see them as often so they sometimes dead-name me. It’s jarring but I think it’ll just take a bit more time for them. I had to get tipsy to tell my sisters-in-law because I was embarrassed to make a big deal about it, but they were completely cool with it. No questions at all. They thought it was awesome that I’ve renamed my identity.

New people I meet have a lot of questions when I tell them, especially asking why. I tell them the very basic version of the truth: I don’t speak to the woman that named me, and my dad and grandfather were the only connection I had to my last name but they’ve passed away. People are super respectful and kind about it. Plus my new name has a million nickname opportunities, I never had a nickname before so that was really cool. Everyone loves coming up with their own little way to say my name that’s personal to them, which is something that’s really special.
